name: Fidel Castro
role: Cuban revolutionary, prime minister (1959–1976) and president (1976–2008)
summary: Castro defended a socialist economy and Communist Party government, with universal public education and health services. He promoted anti-imperialist solidarity and redistribution internationally, and in later life emphasised ecological survival while condemning earlier persecution of gay Cubans.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Article 15 puts only land not held by small farmers or their co-operatives in state hands, and article 20 recognises small farmers' ownership of their land.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Cuba provided military instructors and arms to anti-colonial movements in Africa from the early 1960s, as reported by this account.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He told the UN that Cuba was on the side of the fighting Algerian people against French forces.

capital-controls.rationale: He criticised capital-account liberalisation and called for control of destabilising cross-border financial flows.

central-planning.rationale: The constitution (art. 16) has the state organise and control the whole economy under a single national plan.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He said the working class must struggle against the displaced classes throughout the whole stage of building socialism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He explicitly demanded compensation for Africa and other regions harmed by slavery and colonialism.

conscription.rationale: Article 64 makes military service a duty regulated by law, and Human Rights Watch reports the armed forces conscript from age sixteen.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He blamed wasteful consumer societies for environmental destruction and demanded less luxury consumption.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He defended Cuba’s contribution to fighting apartheid and demanded redress for slavery and colonial exploitation.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In 2010 he called past anti-gay persecution a great injustice and accepted responsibility for failing to stop it.

death-penalty.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports Cuba retains the death penalty for several crimes and added two more in 1999, with the Council of State under Castro as final arbiter.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The constitution (arts. 5, 66) bases the state on party leadership, 'socialist democracy' and democratic centralism, not on open competition among parties.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He called the workers' democracy the 'dictatorship of the proletariat', exercised by the working class over other classes during the building of socialism.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Under articles 71-72 the National Assembly elects the head of state, the President of the Council of State.

dominated-front.rationale: He urged developing states to act together through the Group of 77 and South-South solidarity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He warned of catastrophic atmospheric change and demanded urgent changes in consumption, development and resource allocation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He sought a stronger representative UN with the General Assembly controlling crucial decisions on force.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: He called humanity a species threatened with disappearance and demanded urgent action to avoid ecological self-destruction.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: He proposed a minimum one-percent tax on speculative financial transactions to finance developing countries.

force-without-un.rationale: Cuba sent combat troops to Angola in 1975 and earlier military instructors to Guinea-Bissau on its own decision, with no Security Council authorisation.

free-public-college.rationale: The 1976 constitution (art. 50) guarantees a free school system at every level, with study grants.

future-generations.rationale: He warned that destruction of natural resources indispensable to human life required urgent global action.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Article 14 bases the economy on socialist ownership ending exploitation of man by man, and article 44 pays work by its quality and quantity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He linked Cuba’s lost sovereignty to foreign economic domination and defended revolutionary economic transformation.

independent-unions.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that Cuba permits only one state-controlled union confederation, run by a Politburo member, and has legalised no independent union.

job-guarantee.rationale: Article 44 guarantees work to citizens through the socialist economic system.

leader-cult.rationale: He explicitly opposed official portraits, naming institutions after himself and the deification of leaders.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Article 44 makes work a right, a duty and a matter of honour, and article 63 requires citizens to observe labour discipline.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: He described prostitution as a product of capitalism that socialism ends by rehabilitating prostitutes.

limit-growth.rationale: He demanded sustainable development but explicitly rejected preventing development in the countries needing it most.

limit-population.rationale: He rejected drastic measures to reduce population, arguing that population growth is a result of underdevelopment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He rejected deregulated markets, maximum privatisation and withdrawal of the state as reliable development principles.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He described commercial media and advertising as conditioning thought and manipulating the public.

nation-first.rationale: He placed Cuba’s sovereignty within a demand for international equality and collective action against poverty.

national-resource-control.rationale: He condemned foreign control of Cuba’s land, economy and natural resources as destroying national sovereignty.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said Cuba stood with the peoples who wish to be free, colonial peoples in Africa and Algeria among them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He called a foreign naval base on any country's territory a just cause for concern and demanded the return of Guantanamo, and backed clearing Africa of bases.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 5 makes the Communist Party the leading force of society and the state, and no other party has any constitutional place.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Articles 67-68 make the National Assembly the supreme organ of state power and the only body with constituent and legislative power.

party-controls-media.rationale: Article 52 makes press, radio, television and film state or social property that cannot be private, used to serve the socialist aims.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: His final defence of Cuba tied national dignity to gains in education, science and collective social development.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He said the population explosion is not the cause but the result of underdevelopment.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He argued private press freedom chiefly protects owners’ control over who writes and what is published.

production-for-use.rationale: He rejected leaving national needs to the profit calculations of a handful of large businessmen.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution (arts. 14-15) sets up socialist ownership of the means of production, irreversibly, while protecting only small farmers' land and personal property.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1976 constitution (art. 15) places land not held by small farmers, the subsoil, mines, sugar mills, factories, banks and transport in state ownership 'irreversibly'.

public-service-media.rationale: All media are state or social property under article 52 and used for socialist aims, so no outlet exists free of government editorial control.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Articles 41-42 outlaw and punish discrimination by race and open every office and school to all races.

recall-officials.rationale: Articles 66, 83 and 112 give electors the right to revoke deputies and delegates at any time.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Article 83 lets electors revoke deputies at any time, and article 112 does so for municipal delegates.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He condemned IMF conditions for paralysing social development and demanded removal of the institution.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He demanded regulation of speculative financial institutions and criticised unchecked transnational corporate power.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Article 54 guarantees every person the right to profess any belief and worship under the same law, giving no faith or interpretation precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Article 1 defines Cuba as a socialist state of workers and peasants, with a materialist state outlook, and no nationhood by faith.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He demanded fundamental changes to the international order harming poorer countries’ development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He urged wealthy states to provide effective assistance and praised Cuba’s free international medical and educational programmes.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Article 35 defines marriage as a union of a man and a woman.

second-chamber.rationale: The constitution (arts. 67-69) sets up a single National Assembly with no second chamber.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In 2016 he said Cuba could produce what it needed through its own people’s efforts rather than imperial gifts.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1976 constitution guaranteed freedom of conscience (art. 54) yet had the state educate in a materialist worldview, regulate religious bodies and punish setting faith against the Revolution, and Human Rights Watch reports it was officially atheist until 1992.

separated-powers.rationale: Article 66 establishes the 'unity of power' and article 67 makes the National Assembly the supreme organ of state; courts and prosecutors answer to it and the Council of State (arts. 129-131).

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Article 35 rests marriage on absolute equality of the spouses' rights and duties.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He called developing-country foreign debt unpayable and uncollectable.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He described bourgeois democracy as a system of one class ruling another and replaced it with workers' power over the exploiters.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1976 constitution had the state educate on a materialist conception of the universe (art. 54) while guaranteeing belief; Human Rights Watch reports Cuba was officially atheist until 1992 and later accommodated religion, so the record points both ways.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Human Rights Watch documents prison for 'dangerousness', contempt (desacato), enemy propaganda and sedition against peaceful opponents, and a ban on any independent party or union.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He urged applying science alongside redistribution and changed consumption, rather than technical fixes alone.

term-limits.rationale: The constitution sets no limit on the number of terms of deputies or the President of the Council of State.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Articles 57-58 declare detainees inviolable in person and bar coercion to obtain statements, voiding any forced statement.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Article 16 has the state run the economy by a national plan, and Human Rights Watch reports the one union confederation is state-controlled, so unions do not run it.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1976 constitution (art. 49) guarantees free medical and hospital care to everyone through a state network.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The constitution (arts. 70-72) sets five-year terms with no limit on re-election, and Castro stayed head of state and government from 1976 to 2008.

vanguard-party.rationale: Article 5 defines the Communist Party as the organised Marxist-Leninist vanguard of the working class and leading force of state and society.

women-suffrage.rationale: Article 43 gives women equal political rights with men, and article 136 lets men and women stand for election.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He described international debt, speculation and unequal exchange as mechanisms of exploitation of poorer countries.

notes: Late religious accommodation and his 2010 repudiation of anti-gay persecution govern the relevant answers. Neither establishes a documented position on same-sex marriage. The disputed 2010 remark about the Cuban model is not treated as an unambiguous renunciation of socialism. Media answers follow his explicit later defence of revolutionary political control. Pass of 2026-11-16 (rules 7): answers where a record exists (1976 constitution, Human Rights Watch 1999 report, reports of the Angola deployment) were re-sourced to the record and the earlier words-based or Wikipedia-only versions kept in reviewHistory. Themes searched: economy, government and elections, courts, religion, equality, labour, world and war, colonialism, population. The criminalize-homosexuality answer still rests on his 2010 words; the record on it (UMAP camps, 1979 penal code) is not cited. Two texts were not retrieved (see notFound).
